title: SHAPE of Chain-of-Thought in Math Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2608.28600v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, yet the mathematically meaningful skills underlying their reasoning remain underexplored. We introduce \texttt{SHAPE}, a framework that analyzes Chain-of-Thought (CoT) trajectories through two lenses developed in mathematics education: (1) semantic spaces: the model's evolving mathematical interpretations of a problem (e.g., algebraic, geometric), and (2) heuristics: the specific mathematical actions taken within those spaces (e.g., simplifying the problem, working backward). We first use \texttt{SHAPE} to analyze the reasoning patterns of various models. Our findings reveal that the mathematical heuristics employed by a model better explain final answer correctness than traditional CoT features. translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）在数学推理基准测试中取得了强劲的表现，但其推理背后具有数学意义的技能仍未得到充分探索。我们提出了SHAPE框架，该框架借鉴数学教育领域中的两个视角来分析思维链（CoT）轨迹：（1）语义空间：模型对问题不断演变的数学解读方式（例如代数的、几何的）；（2）启发式方法：模型在这些空间内采取的具体数学行动（例如简化问题、逆向推理）。我们首先利用SHAPE分析了多种模型的推理模式。研究发现，模型所采用的数学启发式方法比传统的CoT特征更能解释最终答案的正确性。此外，模型往往通过将推理精力集中在少数几个语义空间内，而非广泛探索多种空间，来得出正确的解答。
tldr: 该论文提出SHAPE框架，借鉴数学教育中的“语义空间”与“启发式方法”两个视角分析思维链轨迹，发现模型采用的数学启发式方法比传统CoT特征更能解释最终答案的正确性，且成功的推理往往集中在少数语义空间内。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SHAPE, a framework that analyzes Chain-of-Thought trajectories through mathematics education lenses (semantic spaces and heuristics), revealing that a model's mathematical heuristics better explain final answer correctness than traditional CoT features, and successful reasoning tends to concentrate within a few semantic spaces.
